intent: Build PSI-103, the finance CRUD module, continuing the calendar -> kanban -> finance pipeline directly (operator asked for Claude Code, not Hermes, this time).
summary: Implemented /dashboard/finance: types.ts (Zod schemas matching the DB's numeric(16,2) check), actions.ts (list/create/update/delete entries, list categories/boards, upsert category, each permission-gated via requirePermission in try/catch per PSI-102's precedent), lib/format.ts (formatIDR/formatDateWIB). Used the kiranism-shadcn-dashboard skill to learn useDataTable/DataTable/DataTableToolbar since no feature here had used it (0 prior usages). Built columns.tsx (direction/category multiSelect, occurredOn dateRange, amount range with a static [0, 100M] IDR ceiling), entries-table.tsx (reads filters via the same nuqs keys/parsers useDataTable creates internally, since manualFiltering/Pagination/Sorting are hardcoded true -- the caller must fetch already-filtered data), entry-form-dialog.tsx and category-dialog.tsx (Dialog, not Sheet: finance.md wanted Sheet, but the app has zero Sheet forms and five Dialog forms, so I followed the real convention). Added the nav item (Finance, Icons.billing, finance.read) and a kbar action ('Record income or spending' -> /dashboard/finance?new=1, auto-opens the create dialog). Fixed two real bugs found along the way: a PostgREST embedded-select broke because board_id has two possible relationships (boards + the agent_board_status view) -- switched to two follow-up lookups; and Intl.NumberFormat's non-breaking space in currency output, normalized to a plain space. 15 new unit tests (bun test: 43/43). tsc/oxlint/build clean, route registered. Verified live: unauthenticated GET returns a clean 307 to sign-in (no crash); authenticated click-through not run (no seeded dev user at hand), same gap PSI-102 left open.

changes.note: Server Actions: list/create/update/delete entries, list categories/boards, upsert category
Data table column defs with filter meta

decisions.reason: finance.md's original design (written before any code existed) specified Sheet; the actual app has zero Sheet-based forms and five Dialog-based ones (sign-in through invite-user-dialog). Following the real convention over the aspirational doc.
alternatives: Introduce the app's first Sheet-based form

decisions.decision: Two follow-up queries for board/category names instead of an embedded PostgREST select
decisions.reason: finance_entries.board_id has two relationships in the generated types (boards and the agent_board_status view), which breaks the embedded-select's type inference when combined with a second joined table in one select string
alternatives: Pick one relationship name explicitly in the select hint

decisions.decision: Read filter state via the same nuqs keys/parsers the hook creates internally, in the table component itself
decisions.reason: useDataTable hardcodes manualFiltering/manualPagination/manualSorting to true -- it never filters `data` itself, so the caller must fetch already-filtered data; there is no other exposed hook API to read the resulting filter values before the table is constructed
alternatives: Read table.getState().columnFilters via an effect after construction (adds a render round-trip)

decisions.decision: Static [0, 100,000,000] IDR range bound on the amount slider (marked ponytail)
decisions.reason: No real data yet to derive a bound from; a generous static ceiling is fine until entries exist

verification.manual: bun test: 43/43 pass (15 new). Live dev server: unauthenticated GET /dashboard/finance -> 307 to /auth/sign-in?next=%2Fdashboard%2Ffinance (no crash). Authenticated browser walkthrough not run (no seeded dev user with finance.read at hand).

risks: Authenticated UI flow (data table rendering, filters, create/edit/delete round-trip) not exercised by hand -- reviewer should sign in with a finance.read/write user and try it before stamping done

human_review.reason: Authenticated browser walkthrough not run this session; also the first real use of the template's useDataTable system in this app, worth a second look.
